rationale:
The requirement has one testable obligation. With default features, the SDK must expose exactly the listed items, each with the stated Rust item kind and the stated module path. The requirement also says associated items are outside this inventory, and it excludes the hidden `habeas-integration` items.

`crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` is marked `{test}` for this requirement. It covers the obligation as follows:

- **Specified side.** The helper `fn[specified_exports]` reads the `exports` requirement text from the book's `md/requirements/sdk/public-api.md`. It parses each bullet into a (full path, kind) pair using the nesting depth. It rejects malformed entries, odd indentation, skipped parents, non-container parents, a non-crate root, duplicates and an empty inventory.
- **Actual side.** The test runs `cargo doc --no-deps -p trust-but-verify` with default features and with rustflags cleared. It always regenerates the documentation, so stale output can't be used.
- **Documented side.** The helper `fn[documented_exports]` walks rustdoc's item tables recursively, starting at the crate index and following each module. It records the path and kind of every entry. It maps `constant` to `const` and panics on an unknown category or a malformed name. It requires local link targets that exist as files, and it rejects duplicates.
- **Comparison.** The test asserts that both the set difference (missing) and the reverse difference (unexpected) are empty. This enforces "exactly", so an extra public item, a missing item, a wrong kind or a wrong module path would each fail it.

The hidden-items carve-out needs no test. Rustdoc omits hidden items by default. The "following `requirements.sdk.public_api`" clause is cited context. A separate test, `fn[sdk_has_no_public_reexports]`, covers it. It is also marked `{test}` for `public_api`, and I did not reassess it here.

I found no gap.

text: With its default features, `trust-but-verify` exposes exactly the crate and module
items listed below, following {cite}`requirements.sdk.public_api`. Each entry
states its Rust item kind and its name within the enclosing module. Associated
methods, fields, and variants belong to their types' individual contracts.
The internal `habeas-integration` feature supports Habeas interoperability; its
hidden items are outside this supported interface.
Each public SDK item has one defining module path. The SDK exposes no public
re-exports. Its public modules follow the interfaces introduced in these chapters:
- `domain`: application data and the `Domain`, `NodeContents`, and `SourceNodes` traits.
- `graph`: criterion definitions, graph observations, and evidence; `graph::validator`
runs criteria, and `graph::pages` contains paged inspection results.
- `request`: `ValidationContext`, typed `Ask` builders, context values, and request phases.
- `sources`: project inspection, search queries, and their results.
- `outline`: selectable source contents and language rules; `outline::languages`
supplies bundled languages, and `outline::selector` defines selector syntax.
Source access, search engines, redaction, provider transports, and conversation
machinery are implementation details of those interfaces.
